narrative:
Based on the information available, the model has assessed an 84% probability that you represent a bad credit risk, which is why your loan application was denied. This is not a personal judgment, but a statistical evaluation of the factors that historically indicate a higher chance of repayment difficulties.

The most influential factor was the status of your checking account. You currently have a negative balance, whereas most approved applicants either have a positive balance or no checking account at all. A negative balance suggests very limited financial flexibility and often points to immediate cash-flow problems. This was the strongest single signal pushing the decision toward denial.

The second most important factor was the requested loan duration of 60 months. Approved applicants typically request credit for around 19 months on average. A much longer repayment period increases uncertainty, as the bank must carry the risk over a longer time, during which your financial situation could change in unforeseen ways.

The third significant factor was your property status. You reported having no known property or assets. Many approved applicants own real estate, a car, or have savings in building societies or life insurance. Lacking any property means there is no collateral or financial buffer to reassure the bank that the loan could be repaid if your income were interrupted.

To strengthen a future application, you might consider improving your checking account balance and keeping it positive for several months, requesting a smaller loan with a shorter repayment period, and exploring whether you can offer any form of security or a guarantor. These steps would directly address the main concerns that led to this decision.
